thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selection change (fused attention) I'm seeing intermittent OOMs on p3/p4 pools for long-context jobs. Looks like fragmentation + bigger workspace allocations from the new kernels.

maria: Repro locally? what sequence length + batch?

alex: Repro with 32k seq, batch=1, concurrent KV-heavy requests (came up during canary). Profiling with torch.prof and nvtx shows a lot of small frees/allocs and then arena gets forced to expand.

cheng: Do you have the PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF you were testing?

alex: Yep — tried a few knobs to mitigate. Example that avoided the OOMs in my run:

```
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.55,max_split_size_mb:64,expandable_segments:1
```

But note: expandable_segments=1 reduced immediate OOMs by letting segments grow, but increased memory tail and fragmentation in sustained traffic.

maria: Interesting. Did you try lowering garbage_collection_threshold further? that'll force earlier GC of freed blocks and might reduce fragmentation.

alex: Tried 0.4 — OOMs stayed away but latency p99 jumped ~8% under heavy concurrent batching. Looks like more frequent GC stalls.

cheng: From the allocator design perspective: max_split_size_mb controls whether big contiguous blocks can be split. If too small we split more and consume more metadata, too big and we waste space. For our long-context KV cache growth I think bumping to 64/128 helps. expandable_segments helps short term but harms reuse of smaller buffers.

sana: Ran a quick perf matrix on p4d. Baseline (master): tokens/s = 86. With max_split_size_mb=64, garbage_collection_threshold=0.55, expandable_segments=1 -> tokens/s = 82, no OOMs on 32k. With expandable_segments=0 and gc_threshold=0.6 -> tokens/s = 85 but occasional OOM at 32k (1/50 runs).

ryan: So tradeoffs: eliminate OOMs vs p99 latency and throughput. For canary we probably want conservative settings that avoid application OOM even if tokens/s drops a bit. We can also try workspace sizing changes in the kernel to reduce per-request scratch.

alex: Agreed. Proposed plan: 1) Canary config: garbage_collection_threshold=0.55, max_split_size_mb=64, expandable_segments=1 on dedicated long-context model routes only. 2) Instrument allocator metrics + add an alert for arena expansions > X per minute. 3) Parallel work: eng-runtime to explore kernel workspace reuse to avoid per-infer allocations.

maria: I'll add the canary to the rollout with route-based override. Should we gate by cpu/gpu type? only p4/p3?

ryan: limit to p3/p4 pools for now, yes. Also add a perf job that runs 6h long-context stress to catch slow memory growth.

cheng: FYI I dumped the allocator stats after a run — a lot of small free lists never get reused because split policy creates mismatched sizes. We should consider an alternative split heuristic or coalesce pass. That would be less hacky than expandable_segments.

alex: Good note. For short-term canary we'll use the PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF override and monitor. Longer-term we should implement buffer reuse for KV cache and a smarter split/coalesce strategy.

deploy-bot: deploy started by @maria for route:llama-longctx-canary on pool p4-prod-canary :rocket:

maria: Rolling it out now. Will post perf snapshots in #eng-runtime once 1h in.

sana: Quick reminder — include stats: arena_expansions, peak_alloc, fragmentation_ratio in the console dashboard. 

alex: Added to the list. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
